title: Barcelona monitor Kane & Haaland - Wednesday's gossip
description: Barcelona are monitoring Harry Kane and Erling Haaland, Nick Woltemade could be a replacement for Kane at Bayern Munich, and Manchester United are interested in Jarrad Branthwaite, plus more.
fullText:
Barcelona are monitoring both Harry Kane and Erling Haaland, while Germany striker Nick Woltemade could be a replacement for Kane at Bayern Munich, and Manchester United are interested in Jarrad Branthwaite.

Barcelona are looking at England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane, 33, and Manchester City's 26-year-old Norway international Erling Haaland as alternatives to Atletico Madrid and Argentina forward Julian Alvarez, 26. (Talksport)

Bayern Munich have been linked with 24-year-old Newcastle United and Germany forward Nick Woltemade - currently on loan at Juventus - as a potential replacement for Kane. (Talksport)

Manchester United have their sights on Everton and England defender Jarrad Branthwaite, 24, again after his return to action following injury problems. (Football Insider)

English winger Rio Ngumoha, 18, is on Arsenal's radar but Liverpool want to extend his long-term contract. (Athletic - subscription required)

Tottenham remain interested in England and Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White, having previously tried to sign the 26-year-old in summer 2025, but Forest have no intention of selling. (Teamtalk)

Real Madrid striker Endrick could be available in the January transfer window, with Manchester United among those interested in the Brazilian 20-year-old. (AS via Teamtalk)

Spain midfielder Rodri, 30, spoke to Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho "to thank him for his interest and the way he treated me" after joining Barcelona instead of the Bernabeu club from Manchester City in the summer. (Mundo Deportivo - in Spanish)

Barcelona sporting director Deco held a meeting with Brazil international Raphinha, who is under contract until 2028, to discuss extending the 29-year-old forward's deal with the club. (Sport - in Spanish)

AC Milan's option to turn 22-year-old English forward Omari Hutchinson's loan move from Nottingham Forest into a permanent switch is close to 50m euros (£42.8m). (Calciomercato - in Italian)

title: 'I couldn't raise my arm': Texas A&M CB reveals 2025 injury issues
description: On Tuesday, cornerback Dezz Ricks revealed that he played with a torn labrum during the 2025 season.
fullText:
Texas A&M's cornerback rotation is once again led by senior Dezz Ricks, who, after transferring from Alabama before the 2024 season, went from one of the lowest-rated defenders on the roster to a future NFL draft selection with an extremely bright future.

Thanks to coach Mike Elko, new defensive coordinator Lyle Hemphill, and cornerbacks coach Bryant Gross-Armiento, Ricks has played at an elite level in the first two games, allowing just one reception for one yard in five targets in blowout wins over Missouri State and Arizona State.

Per Pro Football Focus, Ricks' 73.7 coverage grade ranks second only to fellow senior starting cornerback Julio Humphrey (83.1), who ranks fifth nationally in PFF's updated cornerback rankings.

On Tuesday, Dezz Ricks, along with starting defensive end T.J. Searcy, spoke to the local media before the Aggies host Kentucky in Week 3, and the former five-star cornerback revealed that he dealt with a serious upper-body injury during the 2025 season, reportedly playing through a torn labrum all year.

Like former starting linebacker Scooby Williams, who played through a torn meniscus during the 2024 season, it's important to remember that Texas A&M's culture under Mike Elko has developed some of the toughest players in the country, and while Dezz Ricks had his moments last season, his struggles in coverage make sense.

More importantly, Tennessee transfer Rickey Gibson struggled in coverage vs. Arizona State, meaning Dezz Ricks and Julio Humphrey will need to keep playing at a high level, along with nickels Jordan Shaw and Bravion Rogers, or the Aggie secondary will not live up to its elite potential.

Texas A&M cornerback Dezz Ricks met with the media today and spoke about Kentucky, being healthy and a lot more. pic.twitter.com/Mvu0jmMt70

title: Bristol Rovers Boss Praises West Ham For £50m Summer Masterstroke: Can They Turn It Into Automatic Promotion?
description: West Ham United have received an endorsement from Bristol Rovers boss Steve Evans, who has praised the club’s hierarchy for keeping a squad together after relegation. Speaking on Sky Sports’ EFL c...
fullText:
West Ham United have received an endorsement from Bristol Rovers boss Steve Evans, who has praised the club's hierarchy for keeping a squad together after relegation. Speaking on Sky Sports' EFL coverage, Evans described the decision as a summer "masterstroke", with captain Jarrod Bowen at the centre of his argument.

As reported by Claret & Hugh, Evans believes the retention of players has given Nuno Espírito Santo a platform that many Championship managers would envy. West Ham sit top after seven league games, and their 6-0 win over Wrexham on 11 September strengthened that position while keeping their promotion push alive.

Evans' warning had plenty of bite. He argued that, given the quality available, finishing outside the automatic promotion places would mean Nuno had failed to meet the season's target. That puts the pressure squarely on the manager, because the board has handed him a squad built to challenge immediately rather than spend a year rebuilding.

"You have first and foremost to give credit to the owners at West Ham because they've kept a tremendous squad of players together for championship football, headed by Jarrod Bowen, who will play a pivotal part.

If Nuno looks at it at the end of the season and they're not in the top two, his objective will have failed because when you look at the squad, most managers would love to have that squad at their disposal"

Evans has a strong point, although the word "failure" needs some context. West Ham United retained Bowen after a relegation that ended their 14-year Premier League stay, and the decision removed one of the risks that usually hits relegated clubs: losing their attacking players and starting again.

LONDON, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 11: Jarrod Bowen of West Ham United celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Sky Bet Championship 2026/27 match between West Ham United and Wrexham at London Stadium on September 11, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Bowen's numbers show why the choice matters. He has started all seven Championship matches, with four league goals and three assists, including a goal and assist in the 6-0 victory over Wrexham. His pace, movement and finishing give West Ham a way through packed defences, especially when matches become tight and opponents protect a point.

Claret & Hugh reported in June that Bowen was the only West Ham player without a 50% relegation wage reduction, while the club pushed to keep key players together. That decision was risky because the wages remain heavy, yet it gives Nuno a core instead of forcing him through another transfer reset.

The evidence says the squad gives Nuno an advantage, but football rarely follows a straight line across 46 matches. Injuries, suspensions, fixture swings and pressure can change the picture. Still, West Ham United have the quality, experience and attacking output to make Evans' top-two demand look reasonable rather than outrageous, and Bowen gives them the sort of match-winner most Championship rivals cannot match.

title: How the Houston Cougars carved out a place in college football over eight decades
description: University of Houston football has changed conferences, coaches and homes over 80 years, but the Cougars may have finally found their place in the Big 12.
fullText:
Join us on a journey to better understand Houston, one question at a time. 

When University of Houston football players followed a candy-red slab out of the tunnel to open the season, the car riding on chrome swangas as Lil' Flip boomed in the background, the clip racked up millions of views and put a national spotlight on the team.

The Cougars are 2-0 after a 77-6 rout of Southern on Saturday and sit at No. 22 in the AP poll, one of five Texas schools in the Top 25 (which is a Lone Star miracle for this #ForeverCoog who has watched the team wade through the waters of mediocrity for nearly a decade). Not only that, they're playing in a Big 12 that survived realignment after UH spent much of its history moving from conference to conference.

That is a long way from where the Cougars were 80 years ago this month, when, on the same patch of Cullen Boulevard, they played their first college football game at a stadium borrowed from Houston ISD and lost to the team that is now known as the Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns.

UH had a mascot almost two decades before the school had a formal football team to go with it.

In 1927, when it was still Houston Junior College, the school hired John R. Bender, a former college coach at Washington State, to teach physical education. Bender put together a volunteer football squad and called it the Cougars in tribute to WSU, whose mascot is also the cougar. (But don't call UH the Cougs. Only Coogs.)

At his urging, students gave the campus newspaper, where this writer cut his teeth, the same name.

Coach Bender died in the summer of 1928, at 46, but the name stuck.

It was not until Sept. 21, 1946, when 11,000 fans filed into HISD's Public School Stadium (which later became Robertson Stadium) to watch Coach Jewell Wallace's team open its first season in the Lone Star Conference against the then-Southwestern Louisiana Institute, that the Cougars became an official, sanctioned college football team.

UH struck first, marching 69 yards on the first drive in program history. Quarterback Charlie Manichia ran 32 yards for the touchdown, the only Cougar scoring play of the game. SLI answered with two late touchdowns to win 13-7, and UH finished that first season 4-6.

Decades of searching for a home followed. In the shadow of schools like UT and A&M, UH hopped from the Lone Star Conference to the Missouri Valley Conference, spent a few years as an independent and then went on a heck of a run in the storied Southwest Conference that produced four titles before the league crumbled in 1996. The Cougars also made stops in middling Conference USA and the American Athletic Conference.

A few years ago, after more than a decade of lobbying from UH administrators and even state leaders, the Big 12 finally came calling.

The first couple of years in the Big 12 were not easy on the Cougars.

UH went 4-8 in 2023, its first year in the conference. That season (and his mediocre performance in the preceding years) cost head coach Dana Holgorsen his job, despite the massive contract buyout he was confident UH couldn't afford.

His replacement, Willie Fritz, went 4-8 again in his first year, but the Cougars broke through in 2025 with a 10-3 record, a 38-35 Texas Bowl win over LSU and a No. 22 ranking to finish the year.

The next test for these Cougars on the come-up comes Friday night in Lubbock, where No. 22 UH faces No. 13 Texas Tech in the first meeting between the teams as ranked opponents since 1978.

UH hasn't beaten Texas Tech since the Case Keenum era, when a last-minute touchdown run in 2009 gave the Cougars their most recent win over the Red Raiders.

Perhaps victory on Friday could give the Coogs something to celebrate the next time they roll a slab out of the tunnel.

There's more to Houston with the Chronicle. 

This article originally published at How the Houston Cougars carved out a place in college football over eight decades.

title: Darius Taylor’s uncertain status creates golden opportunity for A.J. Turner
description: Minnesota's running back is already banged up heading into its Week 3 matchup with Akron.
fullText:
The Gophers' oft-injured running back Darius Taylor was already limited to just 14 offensive snaps in Week 2 against Mississippi State. P.J. Fleck has referred to his status as "day-to-day," but anyone who has followed Fleck's team knows that could mean a lot of different things. The uncertainty could open the door for A.J. Turner.

Turner was a highly-touted transfer portal pickup for Minnesota heading into the 2025 season. He led all of FBS-qualified running backs with 8.3 yards per carry in his final season at Marshall. 247Sports ranked him as the 144th-best player and eighth-best running back in the transfer portal after the 2024 season.

He had four games with more than 100 rushing yards in 2024, and he finished with 104 carries for 864 yards and eight total touchdowns. He looked like a player who could make the jump to the next level.

We didn't get a real look at how his talent would transfer from the Sun Belt to the Big Ten last season. He played just 22 offensive snaps before suffering a season-ending injury in Week 3 against Cal. He compiled 16 carries for 64 yards and one touchdown, but he never had more than six carries in a single game.

Turner returned to the field against Mississippi State last week for the first time since that trip to Cal. He had two carries for four yards and one reception for five yards on 16 total snaps. With stud freshman Ryan Estrada out for the season and Taylor clearly banged up, there's an opportunity for Turner to have a bigger role in Week 3 against Akron.

If Taylor's injury is minor, it still might behoove Minnesota to rest him against an inferior opponent in Week 3 before traveling to Washington for the Big Ten opener in Week 4. It could also give Turner an opportunity to get back into game speed.

Elon transfer TJ Thomas has gotten off to a solid start in his Gophers' career, but he's just 5-foot-8, and he might not be built for a true bell cow role in the Big Ten. A two-headed approach with Turner could be Minnesota's best strategy if Taylor is not able to go.

The Gophers' running game has been stuck in neutral for the last four seasons under offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. Turner could provide them with a spark at the perfect time.

title: Despite Week 1 loss, one group on the Browns offense improved
description: Looking at the offensive snap counts from the Browns’ Week 1 loss to the Jaguars.
fullText:
The Cleveland Browns played a terrible game in Week 1, with a lot of blame going to QB Deshaun Watson on offense, and then the team's defense in general. But were other areas responsible for the low output offensively too? There was one unit that actually played at a very high level, believe it or not.

Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns' Week 1 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

16-of-22 (72.7%) for 205 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT. 6 carries, 38 yards (6.3 YPC), 1 fumble.

We can't just look at the stat line for Deshaun Watson and think he wasn't a problem. With that said, there are two sides to this. Fans are fed up with Watson. We thought we were done with him after the owner's comments last year, and yet here he is, starting again. How many empty scoring halves of offense under Watson have we been subjected to? And then when you listen to the clip below, they're exactly right, what the hell are we doing here, Todd Monken? We are coddling Watson with kid gloves.

"Listen to that. It that not something you'd say to your QB in 6th grade? I'm serious. We're all gonna have to deal with it for the rest of the season. This is just an abomination." 

🚨 @KenCarman to @SportsBoyTony on #Browns head coach Todd Monken's comments on Deshaun Watson's… pic.twitter.com/thcnHKHElX

Now, with all of that in mind, sure, there were a few positives I saw from Watson. I thought his deep ball in garbage time was thrown well, and he had some nice scrambles. He is certainly not tentative about running after his two Achilles injuries. The problem is, this is what, year four of us seeing Watson with the Browns? We're sick of trying to cherry pick a few highlights to hope he'll be better. That's stuff you'd want to point out with Shedeur Sanders as a youngster, not Watson at this point, who has proven he is too turnover prone and doesn't put points on the board.

12 carries, 33 yards (2.8 YPC). 2 catches, 17 yards (2 targets).

1 carry, 1 yard (1.0 YPC). 3 catches, 25 yards (3 targets).

The Browns were blown out so early that it again made it difficult to rely on the running game. Also, this is a Jaguars front that thrived at stopping the run a year ago.

Nonetheless, there was nothing really special about the way Quinshon Judkins ran in Week 1. His backup, Dylan Sampson, is out with an injury now.

Fullback Michael Burton got six snaps in.

2 catches, 59 yards (4 targets), 1 TD.

4 catches, 43 yards (5 targets). 3 carries, 15 yards (5.0 YPC), 1 fumble.

2 catches, 26 yards (4 targets).

Despite his fumble, I liked that KC Concepcion was utilized in a variety of ways like he was in the preseason. Based on touches, he was the most involved receiver by far.

Denzel Boston caught two passes, including a deep ball for a touchdown. You can see the frame he has and how Browns quarterbacks will be confident in throwing the ball his direction, thinking it'll either be a catch of a contested play, but not an interception.

Concepcion and Boston received decent grades for Cleveland from PFF in the high 60s, making them the team's second- and third-highest graded players offensively.

It was surprising to see Tylan Wallace receive 29% of the snaps. I didn't think he'd even be involved in the offense. He even out-snapped Isaiah Bond, who had seemed to have a solid camp for Cleveland.

2 catches, 21 yards (3 targets).

Harold Fannin wasn't even looked at until late in the second half. Ridiculous.

Blake Whiteheart caught the opening pass, but didn't have anything else come his way. Cleveland only went with two tight ends getting reps.

Austin Barber was the Browns' highest-graded player, per PFF, receiving a grade of 82.6. You get the feeling that he'll remain at right guard, even when Teven Jenkins returns.

Overall, the new Browns' offensive line blocked well. However, the penalties stacked up and were killers.

PFF is attributing all 5 of the Jaguars' sacks to Deshaun Watson, and 0 being on the offensive line. The offensive line and wide receiver play remain encouraging, if we're looking for optimism moving forward.

PFF credits all Browns offensive linemen with allowing ZERO sacks. Deshaun Watson was sacked 5 times, which means PFF is attributing all 5 sacks to the quarterback. pic.twitter.com/wMlENfI8qF

ESPN agreed in their assessment of the Browns' offensive line:

Despite the Browns' struggles on offense in Week 1, Cleveland's offensive line graded out well in ESPN's blocking metrics:

🏈 T-3rd in pass block win rate
🏈 7th in run block win rate

Both metrics measure how often offensive lines successfully sustain their blocks for at least…

title: Maikel Garcia returns to the roster
description: The Royals’ lineup received a boost today with the reinstatement of infielder Maikel Garcia from the Injured List. Garcia had been out since August 20 with a hamstring injury. It has been a frustrating year for the 26-year-old, coming of an All-Star season in 2025 and a five-year, $57 million contract extension last winter. After […]
fullText:
The Royals' lineup received a boost today with the reinstatement of infielder Maikel Garcia from the Injured List. Garcia had been out since August 20 with a hamstring injury.

It has been a frustrating year for the 26-year-old, coming of an All-Star season in 2025 and a five-year, $57 million contract extension last winter. After a strong start, he injured his hand in mid-May against the Cardinals. He played through the injury, but went into a slump, batting .232 with no home runs in 29 games before he finally landed on the Injured List on June 23. He returned to action on August 17, but injured his hamstring just four days later. Overall, he is hitting .269/.324/.385 with three home runs in 73 games. Despite his limited action, he has been worth 1.6 fWAR, 22nd-most among all third baseman.

To make room on the roster, the Royals optioned outfielder Matthew Lugo to Triple-A Omaha. The 25-year-old appeared in nine games and went 2-for-14 (.143) with a walk.

title: Joey Porter Jr. Trade Rumors: Top NFL Insider Says Steelers Fans Should Monitor These Teams
description: The Steelers could have multiple suitors if they decide to move Joey Porter Jr.
fullText:
Joey Porter Jr. Trade Rumors: Top NFL Insider Says Steelers Fans Should Monitor These Teams originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh. Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Amid an unresolved contract situation, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport identified the Chiefs and Lions as two teams to watch if Pittsburgh ultimately decides to trade Joey Porter Jr.

Rapoport's comments on Tuesday's edition of "The Pat McAfee Show" come as the Steelers remain at an impasse with their cornerback over a contract extension. They have reportedly indicated they are willing to listen to trade offers.

"The Steelers have said that Joey Porter Jr is ramping up and then there's the contract part of it..

There are some teams that need corners and he's a very good player..

Pittsburgh has been open to trading him..

I would keep an eye on the Chiefs and Lions"@RapSheet#PMSLivepic.twitter.com/mJEgXxhzlO

Porter missed Pittsburgh's Week 1 win over Atlanta after dealing with a back injury. Head coach Mike McCarthy said the decision to keep Porter inactive was his, citing Porter's limited preparation.

While Rapoport didn't say a trade is imminent, Detroit's interest in Porter appears to be legitimate. The Lions have reportedly approached Pittsburgh about a potential trade.

Detroit's secondary was exposed in the second half of its Week 1 win over the Saints, allowing six completions of at least 20 yards. Saints wide receiver Chris Olave finished with 10 catches for 182 yards, highlighting the need for a cornerback capable of holding up against opposing No. 1 receivers.

Sports Illustrated's John Maakaron identified Detroit as the team best suited to make a "splash trade" for the Steelers cornerback, pointing to Porter's ability to play press-man coverage and hold his own without safety help. That would give defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard more flexibility to use aggressive pressure packages.

The Chiefs have a clear need at cornerback after trading Trent McDuffie to the Rams during the offseason. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who was selected with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, suffered a shoulder injury after intercepting Bo Nix on Monday night.

"If Delane is hurt, [Chiefs general manager] Brett Veach will make a trade," Rapoport said. "He'll be risky. He'll make a trade."

Porter's contract demands could make a potential trade complicated because of the Chiefs' tight cap situation. He's entering the final year of his rookie deal, meaning any team trading for him would need to consider the cost of a long-term extension in addition to the draft capital or players being sent out.

title: Sean McVay defends Quentin Lake's performance vs. 49ers: 'Did a great job'
description: Quentin Lake allowed seven catches on 10 targets, but he also had a pick and two total passes defensed against the 49ers.
fullText:
In their season-opening loss, Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake was targeted in coverage several times as the San Francisco 49ers appeared to repeatedly test his skills as a coverage defender.

While Lake did secure an interception, he also allowed seven catches on 10 targets for 54 yards, many of them coming on touchdown-scoring drives for the 49ers. His performance was unusual for a player who's been called the linchpin of their defense, especially after the team added Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in the offseason.

Lake wasn't the only defensive back who had a little bit of a tough day, as the unit suffered multiple failures against the 49ers' elite offensive attack. Head coach Sean McVay spoke about the job his captain did on Thursday, surprisingly stating he thought Lake played well, while alluding to the coaching staff needing to do a better job of positioning players in better spots.

"I thought 'Q' did a great job," said McVay. "'Q' is active. He has a bunch of different roles that he's playing for us. His communication, his ownership, his understanding. That pick was a great play by him. Then he was really active in the run game. He's going to continue to be a big factor.

In the contest, the 49ers had 379 yards of total offense, with 174 being rushing yards.

"I don't think really the game the other day was really any sort of reflection of the way that we want to play in any of the three phases on a consistent basis, even though there were some positive things that we saw," McVay continued. "I'm excited about how we can say, 'Hey, what does that identity look like as we continue to establish it, learn about this team? How do we put them in the most favorable spots and then how can our play style come to life where we can play complementary ball off of one another?' The other day, like I told you guys, one of those humbling days. We correct it. We look at ourselves in the mirror and we say, 'How can we move forward and be a part of the solution?' And it's exactly what you're going to get from this group."

Perhaps Lake's bad day was due to the Rams being outcoached. In the end, it doesn't matter. How Lake and the Rams' secondary respond in Week 2 will be a turning point for how this season unfolds. If things are fixed against the New York Giants, no harm, no foul.

However, if there are issues again, McVay may be forced to provide a real answer to the lingering issues. Either it's Lake, or it's the scheme – or it's both. The good news is that it could also be neither, and last Thursday was a one-off. With some film on their opponents, Los Angeles has exactly what it needs to change the narrative surrounding the defense.

This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Sean McVay defends Quentin Lake's performance vs. 49ers: 'Did a great job'

title: Mets predicted to trade 13 home run infielder to AL Central club in offseason
description: Big changes are coming to the Mets.
fullText:
Mets predicted to trade 13 home run infielder to AL Central club in offseason originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The New York Mets should be a very active team this offseason.

On Monday, the NL East club was eliminated from postseason contention for the second consecutive year.

With players like Juan Soto and Francisco Lindor, that's wildly disappointing for everyone involved.

If the Mets decide to make significant roster changes, first baseman Mark Vientos could be one of the players on the move.

FanSided's Jake Elman wrote that the Mets need an upgrade over Vientos at first base, especially after the failed Jorge Polanco experiment.

The 26-year-old could provide value to a rebuilding team.

"Vientos has managed -1.3 bWAR since the start of last season, and he's since moved from third to first. His versatility as a corner infielder and his affordability — he's under team control through 2030 — could make him an appealing buy-low option for a rebuilding club," Elman wrote.

Vientos is hitting .214 with 13 home runs and a .667 OPS in 2026, two seasons after posting career highs in homers (27) and OPS (.837).

Elman predicts that the right-handed hitter's next destination will be the Minnesota Twins.

"Although the Yankees also came to mind, we'll predict Vientos lands in the Twin Cities. Josh Bell is a pending free agent, which could open DH reps for either Vientos or first baseman Royce Lewis," Elman added. "He's not the flashiest name for the Twins, but he'll likely come relatively cheap."

MORE: Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski makes all kinds of MLB history with 1,000 pitches of 100 mph

Connecting Vientos to the New York Yankees is an odd thing to do unless he transitions back to third base.

With Luis Garcia Jr. and Ben Rice under contract, the Yankees are set at first. However, a platoon partner for Ryan McMahon at third wouldn't be the worst idea.

Vientos would be a low-cost option for the Twins, but it's unclear if the Mets will even entertain trade offers.

title: Patriots Power Rankings: Week 2 vs. Steelers “a must win”?
description: Check out where the experts ranked the Patriots heading into Week 2
fullText:
Welcome to the season opening column for the 2026 Patriots Power Rankings. Preseason rankings aren't worth the trouble as there are too many hypotheticals too far away from games that count. Those opinions may prove correct, but there's no Win-Loss results to measure them by. They're a fine excuse to offer some thoughts about each team, but they're more of a suggestion than a ranking.

That said, after the Week 1 loss in Seattle New England sits at a hard 0-1, third in the AFC East and ranked between 8th and 19th. The Jets are 1-0 and first in the division. Former head coach Bill Parcells famously said, "You are what your record says you are" but he wasn't referring to Week 1 rankings whispering sweet nothings in his ear.

Conor Orr and Frank Schwab had the more positive takes below, while Mike Florio added his signature snark and Pete Prisco called the upcoming match against the Steelers "a must win." [Insert eye-roll emoji here]. It may be early but the hyperbole is in mid-season form.

The Steelers won last week … vs. the Falcons, but I think they're beatable. Pats win and cover the (4.5) spread.

New York Jets (1-0) vs. Green Bay Packers (0-1)

Buffalo Bills (1-0) vs. Detroit Lions (1-0)

New England Patriots (0-1) vs. Pittsburgh Steelers (1-0)

Miami Dolphins (0-1) at San Francisco 49ers (0-1)

Baltimore Ravens (1-0) vs. New Orleans Saints (0-1)

Jacksonville Jaguars (0-1) at Denver Broncos

Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-1)

Cincinnati Bengals (1-0) at Houston Texans (0-1)

Kansas City Chiefs vs. Indianapolis Colts (0-1)

Tennessee Titans (0-1) vs. Philadelphia Eagles (1-0)

Cleveland Browns (0-1) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1)

8th – Bradley Locker (PFF): Last year's AFC champions turned heads thanks to the exemplary performance of Drake Maye, who received a worthwhile boost in the form of Brown entering his third pro season. The Patriots' defense rode a scintillating finish to end the year third in EPA per play and points per drive, with a lockdown secondary serving as the anchor. New England has been fraught with doubt all offseason — in part due to a questionable pass rush and run game — but will be in the mix to get back to the playoffs with the 13th-easiest schedule.

9th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): The Patriots had a bad draw in their Seahawks' Super Bowl rematch in Seattle but still had a chance to win the game late with more impressive defense. The pressure is on early with the Steelers, Jaguars and Bills next on the schedule.

10th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Non-QB newcomer debut: Edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones. Signed to a three-year, $36.5 million deal in free agency, the eight-year veteran totaled four QB hits, one sack and two tackles. He was generally a solid presence setting the edge in the running game, as well. The Patriots targeted Jones over retaining K'Lavon Chaisson, who led the team with 7.5 sacks last season. Runner-up choice: Sixth-round rookie linebacker Namdi Obiazor (TCU), who led the team with three special teams tackles, including one on the opening kickoff. — Mike Reiss.

10th – Nate Davis (USA Today): QB Drake Maye has four multi-interception games in his three-year career, half of them in his past two starts against Seattle. But, hey, at least he wasn't hit nearly as much in the opener as he was in Super Bowl 60.

10th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): Three interceptions by Drake Maye, an injury that will cost WR A.J. Brown a month, and they couldn't beat a Seahawks team led by Drew Lock. Unfortunately, their schedule won't get any easier.

11th – Conor Orr (SI): Drake Maye is primed for a silence-all-doubters game this week after throwing one of the most ill-advised situational balls of the last few regular seasons. Of course, the way opening week played out, New England is tasked with both an emotional exorcism this week against a bad Steelers team and a schematic streamlining. Luckily, it doesn't look like Pittsburgh is posing much of a threat.

11th – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): The overreaction directed at Drake Maye proves that the hate of the Patriots hasn't died just because Bill Belichick and Tom Brady are long gone. Maye didn't play well in the opener and didn't have a good postseason either. He played elite defenses in almost every game though. Maye is going to be good. He's just not able to overcome a middling supporting cast — A.J. Brown was out for the second half and TreVeyon Henderson was inactive in the opener — against great defenses as a third-year player. He's not nearly as bad as you'll read on social media.

13th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): Fortunately, blowing it twice in the same game counts as only one loss.

18th – Eric Edholm (NFL): Drake Maye's three interceptions clearly contributed to New England's meltdown in Seattle, but the quarterback wasn't the lone culprit in the 13-10 defeat. The Patriots' defense allowed backup QB Drew Lock to lead the Seahawks on two fourth-quarter scoring drives, and Mike Vrabel's team wilted under the pressure applied by the reigning champs. Now New England is staring at a month (or longer) without A.J. Brown. The Pats will need to bounce back quickly to fight off the allegations of being soft-schedule merchants.

19th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): Drake Maye has struggled against good defenses, which he did in the opener against Seattle. This week's game with the Steelers feels like a must-win for the Patriots.

title: Kansas flag football rankings: USA TODAY Sports Super 10
description: Kansas high school flag football is officially a varsity sport. See which teams top the inaugural Super 10 rankings.
fullText:
Kansas made history this summer, joining 23 other states in officially sanctioning flag football as a high school varsity sport. As new athletes across the state gear up for the inaugural season, Kansas is helping make the sport one of the fastest-growing sports in the country.

Now, the flag football season is officially underway, and teams across the state are showing off the talent they have to offer.

With some teams already off to undefeated starts and others still waiting to take the field, the season is just beginning — and there is plenty of football left to be played.

title: Vanderbilt football's future starts now: Jared Curtis takes over at QB
description: Clark Lea announced Sept. 15 that 5-star true freshman Jared Curtis will start at quarterback against NC State in Week 3.
fullText:
Vanderbilt football is making a quarterback change.

Commodores coach Clark Lea announced Tuesday, Sept. 15, he's handing the offense to true freshman Jared Curtis against NC in Week 3. Curtis is a former five-star recruit and highest-ranked prospect in program history.

Vanderbilt started veteran Blaze Berlowitz in its first two wins against Austin Peay and Delaware this season, but he largely struggled before being replaced by Curtis in the 35-26 win against the Blue Hens in Week 2.

What we're hearing: Drew Mestemaker's draft stock, Lane Kiffin has spotlight

Curtis completed 14-of-22 passes for 210 yards with a touchdown in the win, also rushing for three scores. He played sparingly in the season opener, although he threw for 60 yards on 7-for-9 passing.

"He's earned it, he's worked really hard," Lea told reporters. "Obviously, on Saturday, the first drive I think it showed some things were part of the concerns, just through training camp some of the operational issues. But we really wanted coming out of last week to get him in early and get him a couple of series back-to-back.

"The idea that he was able to score a touchdown on that first drive with all the issues, I mean, that was impressive. As he settled in the game, I thought the game really slowed down for him."

The Nashville native has been viewed as the Commodores' future at the position since he flipped his commitment from Georgia before the early signing period started last year. He was the No. 4-ranked player nationally and No. 2 quarterback of the 2026 recruiting class, per 247Sports' Composite rating.

Delaware took a 17-14 lead into halftime against Vanderbilt before Curtis entered and led the Commodores on three scoring drives in the third quarter. Vanderbilt was also held to 28 points against FCS Austin Peay in the season opener.

Vanderbilt, which won 10 games last season with Heisman Trophy runner-up Diego Pavia at the helm, is hoping to keep its momentum moving forward as a program. Curtis fulfilling his projection as one of the best prospects in the country would certainly help.

Here's a look at Curtis' game-by-game stats this season, along with highlights from his extended action against Delaware:

vs. Austin Peay: 7-of-9 passing for 60 yards; three carries for 22 yards

vs. Delaware: 14-of-22 passing for 210 yards; eight carries for a yard with two touchdowns

WHAT A CATCH 👀#SCTop10 pic.twitter.com/H3K57fQ8Yf

Curtis was the No. 4-ranked player in the 2026 recruiting class, per 247Sports' Composite rankings. He was the No. 2-rated quarterback, only behind current Tennessee starter Faizon Brandon, another true freshman starter in the SEC.

Curtis' reported offers list is filled with top-tier programs, from Georgia, Alabama, Ohio State, Texas, Oregon and Indiana, to name a few.

title: Mike Vrabel's honest reaction to Patriots WR Romeo Doubs' dropped pass
description: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel commented on wide receiver Romeo Doubs' crucial dropped pass late in the game against the Seahawks.
fullText:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel stood up for veteran wide receiver Romeo Dobbs after his disappointing performance against the Seattle Seahawks in last week's season opener.

Doubs finished the game with zero receptions on three targets. One of those targets was a wide-open pass from quarterback Drake Maye that would have been a major first-down conversion late in the game.

Maye threw an interception after the dropped pass.

Doubs' struggles are even more glaring considering that the team signed him to a four-year, $68 million deal in free agency. The team will also be playing without star wide receiver A.J. Brown for the foreseeable future after he was placed on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain.

"He dropped a pass," Vrabel told media members, via Patriots Wire's Sophie Weller. "Everybody drops a pass, everybody misses a tackle... did a lot of great things during camp, just like everybody did. so I know he's excited to get back out there."

Mike Vrabel on Romeo Doubs:

"He dropped a pass. Everybody drops a pass, everybody misses a tackle... did a lot of great things during cam, just like everybody did. so I know he's excited to get back out there."

It's important to keep in mind that Doubs didn't play during the preseason, and it was only the first week of the regular season. He will have an opportunity to contribute to change the narrative by stepping up as Maye's No. 1 option with Brown out.

A potential bounce-back game lies on the horizon with the Pittsburgh Steelers next on the schedule in Week 2.

title: Minnesota Vikings Legend Makes Strong Kyler Murray Comments
description: The Minnesota Vikings entered Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers with excitement about new starting quarterback Kyler Murray. That excitement was short-lived after Murray went down with a concussion early in the first quarter. Murray only attempted five passes during the game. He completed three of those attempts for 18 yards, but also threw […] The post Minnesota Vikings Legend Makes Strong Kyler Murray Comments appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The Minnesota Vikings entered Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers with excitement about new starting quarterback Kyler Murray. That excitement was short-lived after Murray went down with a concussion early in the first quarter.

Murray only attempted five passes during the game. He completed three of those attempts for 18 yards, but also threw an ill-advised interception off of his back foot. Carson Wentz entered the game and played well in relief.

During his NFL career, Murray has shown flashes of superstar potential. Unfortunately, those flashes have not been turned into consistency. There are some who think the Vikings would be better off making the switch from Murray to Wentz moving forward.

Despite those opinions, one Minnesota legend has spoken out with strong comments about Murray as the Vikings' quarterback.

During an appearance on the "Fully Loaded Podcast" on Monday, Carter made his feelings about Murray's starting status crystal clear.

"They're not better off without Kyler Murray," Carter said. "Carson Wentz had less than 150 yards passing, and he played over three quarters. Now Justin Jefferson, after an offseason last year when we only had two touchdowns, he cracks two touchdowns in the first week."

Carter continued on, revealing more about his opinion that Murray is the best option for Minnesota as starting quarterback.

"They were very crafty as far as getting him into open space so he can make some plays. But Kyler Murray, this is set up for him. So, after this concussion, how many weeks is it going to take for him to get back in there?"

Following those comments, Carter also spoke out about Wentz and how he sees the veteran quarterback at this stage of his career.

"They got the Bears this week, but Carson Wentz came to do exactly what if somebody gets banged up: I can start for you for two, three, four weeks," Carter said. "I can get you a couple wins, but I'm a backup at this stage of my career."

Everyone is entitled to their own opinion. Some believe that Wentz gives the Vikings a better chance to run an offense they're more comfortable with. Murray is the better playmaker and some believe that he should get back on the field as the starter as soon as he's ready to play.

Only time will tell, but the most likely scenario still seems to be Murray resuming his starting job when he's cleared to return from the concussion.

title: South Walton's Neely Kight commits to Miami women's golf
description: Following a state title her freshman year and back-to-back impressive postseasons, SoWal junior Neely Kight has committed to the University of Miami.
fullText:
SANTA ROSA BEACH — With the Hurricanes full-send on Neely Kight, the decision to commit wasn't so much why Miami?

The year-round beautiful weather. The facilities at Biltmore Golf Course. The coaching staff of Janice Olivencia and assistant Jim Garren.

To Kight, considered one of the top 50 golfers of the 2028 class and on the short list of state title contenders in the Sunshine State, it was an easy decision to commit to the Hurricanes in the midst of her junior year.

Vote now: FPL Athlete of the Week for Sept. 7-12

"I think the biggest thing for me was the coaches, coach Janice and coach Jim, they're phenomenal people and they're really creating such a great program down there in Miami," Kight said. "And obviously the weather is great for golfing, and I just really like the program that they've started and continue to build. I'm really excited."

Kight is coming off back-to-back incredible campaigns as an underclassman. As a freshman, she shot 78-72 at state to finish seventh individually and lead the Seahawks to their first-ever state title on her way to shoring up Daily News Golfer of the Year honors. Then last year, Kight shot 77-74 to finish 15th at state.

This offseason she had a few notable victories, including the Tuscaloosa Junior Championship with a 3-under 210 over three days. That included an opening-round 66.

Miami, after finishing 10th in last year's ACC Championship with no individual top-30 finishes, clearly took notice of the red numbers and Kight's limitless potential.

But Kight still has two years of high school golf left. And she's looking to join North Florida commit Lily Martin, who led the second round at state before finishing three back with a 1-over 143, in leading South Walton back to the top of the state podium.

"She and I are really good friends and we practice a lot together," Kight said. "Our team will go to state again, like the last two years, and I think the goal is to win state as a team. Obviously me and her want the individual win as well. For sure, we're always competing for that."

After an offseason highlighted by wins, red numbers and her Miami commitment, a lot is working well for Kight. She's striping the ball 260 yards off the tee. She's in love with her 8- and 9-irons, to the point where everything 150 yards and in she feels dialed to sticking it within 10 feet. And her short game has seen tremendous growth, especially with her putter.

Miami is getting an elite golfer with LPGA potential. Kight is getting her dream school.

"I feel like Miami has been our No. 1 pick for a long time, just because of the way they've recruited me," Kight said. "They did a really good recruiting me and making me feel wanted, so I feel like the whole family really wanted me to go there. My sister, my parents are very proud of me, so we're all really excited."

This article originally appeared on Northwest Florida Daily News: South Walton's Neely Kight commits to Miami women's golf

title: Behind the Last-Ditch Lobbying Battle Over the Bipartisan Senate College Sports Bill
description: An opposition coalition has formed to block the bill.
fullText:
As a final vote on the Protect College Sports Act (PCSA) draws near, lobbying efforts have gone into overdrive.

Senators are scheduled to convene on the floor on Tuesday afternoon to advance the bill to a final vote on the Senate floor. Ahead of the votes, multiple sources told FOS this week they expect the bill to get the necessary 60 votes. But lawmakers in favor of the bill face an opposition coalition that has formed to block them.

The result: a week of dueling press conferences, competing ESPN segments, and involvement from powerful labor and civil rights groups. College coaches visited Capitol Hill, while players have found themselves on both sides of the debate. Behind the scenes, private strategizing and negotiating have continued.

The PCSA, the result of years of negotiations and tens of millions of dollars in federal lobbying, would be the first college sports bill to reach a full floor vote, let alone pass in either chamber of Congress.

It would double the current revenue-sharing cap on college sports but implement stricter NIL (name, image, and likeness) rules, institute a one-time transfer portal, and codify eligibility standards. It would also codify some health and safety standards and require the richest schools to maintain women's and Olympic sports roster numbers. A second section of the bill would allow schools to pool and sell media rights, prevent a power conference super league, and forbid conferences from expanding beyond 19 teams. A third section would fund broadband service at historically Black colleges and universities.

Since the September recess, co-sponsors Sens. Ted Cruz (R., Texas), Maria Cantwell (D., Wash.), and Eric Schmitt (R., Mo.) have worked to ensure the bill gets to 60 votes, one Senate aide tells FOS.

The White House has been involved as well, beyond public statements of support from President Donald Trump. White House college sports committee members Cody Campbell (Texas Tech board chairman and booster) and Randy Levine (New York Yankees president) have been key members of the lobbying effort.

Meanwhile, a left-leaning coalition has formed against the bill. Sens. Chris Murphy (D., Conn.) has spearheaded public opposition, with Sen. Corey Booker (D., N.J.) quietly assisting. In addition, labor groups including the AFL-CIO (and its sports council, which includes 10 professional sports unions) and SEIU, as well as civil rights groups, including the NAACP, have begun using their lobbying power against the legislation. They have argued college athletes should have collective bargaining rights to establish rules, rather than Congress, and have raised civil rights issues with capping athlete pay in basketball and football.

One Democratic Senate aide tells FOS that "democratic offices are hearing serious concerns about this bill from important stakeholders," and that "opposition to the bill is growing."

An informal group of agents has also have sprung up as detractors as well, according to two sources.

To complicate matters further, bill supporters are juggling an array of stakeholders requesting revisions. Several right-leaning advocacy groups (and a few senators) said the bill could override state laws banning transgender athletes from competing in women's sports—an issue senators have fixed, sources said. No major changes have been made to other aspects of the bill, however, including the expansion provision.

One of the biggest lobbying battlegrounds this week is playing out on ESPN's airwaves.

On Saturday, Cruz sat for a nine-minute interview on College GameDay. But it backfired—both he and ESPN faced backlash for the segment. Since then, ESPN has agreed to platform a detractor: During Tuesday's 6 p.m. SportsCenter, NAACP CEO Derrick Johnson will appear to lay out his concerns with the legislation.

Also this weekend, fans saw ads lobbying for the bill funded by Campbell's organization, Saving College Sports. The commercials, part of a $10 million campaign, have run each week and have already featured Saban and Colorado Buffaloes football coach Deion Sanders. Neither Sanders nor Saban were paid to appear in these ads, FOS previously reported.

Then, on Monday, came the onslaught of press conferences.

Around midday, the labor groups, the NAACP, and college athlete advocacy organizations teamed up for a Zoom press conference criticizing the bill. Players, including Maryland women's basketball player Oluchi Okananwa, LSU women's basketball player Jada Williams, and Temple football player Jackson Pruitt, said they wanted rules and regulations in college sports just as much as coaches and administrators—but that they wanted to be involved in the negotiating process through collective bargaining.

"Athletes don't want this," Pruitt said. "And truth be told, athletes aren't fully educated on what's taking place. And they weren't vetted about this."

Players also raised concerns about loopholes in health and safety standards and prohibitions on players suing schools or governing bodies. Marty McNair, the father of late Maryland football player Jordan McNair, who died from heat stroke after a Maryland football practice in 2018, agreed with them.

Four hours later, senators held a press conference in support of the bill featuring a separate group of elite men's basketball coaches, including Arkansas' John Calipari, Gonzaga's Mark Few, and Houston's Kelvin Sampson. Executive directors of the American Football Coaches Association and National Association of Basketball Coaches were also in attendance.

Coaches said they supported the transfer limits and eligibility restrictions the bill would provide. "You can sense the desperation in everybody's voices. We really, really need help. And we need it from Congress," Few said. "This bill is the best possible thing we can do right now for college athletics."

More than a dozen college athletes joined to voice their support, mostly suggesting that the bill would protect the Olympic pipeline and preserve women's and Olympic sports opportunities.

"Athletes in Olympic sports deserve protected programs. We deserve continued education. And we deserve the chance to represent America on an Olympic world stage," Michigan rower Sophia Stylianos said. "The Protect College Sports Act preserves this Olympic pipeline and the integrity of non-revenue and Olympic sport athletes."

The post Behind the Last-Ditch Lobbying Battle Over the Bipartisan Senate College Sports Bill appeared first on Front Office Sports.

title: Vanderbilt football injury update on Cole Spence, Aaron Bryant, Jaylin Lackey
description: Here are Vanderbilt football injury updates going into the NC State game, including Cole Spence, Jaylin Lackey and Aaron Bryant.
fullText:
Vanderbilt football will be without Aaron Bryant for the remainder of the 2026 season due to a torn ACL, Clark Lea announced Sept. 15.

Jaylin Lackey and Cole Spence are also out for the game against NC State, while Jamison Curtis is "week to week." Lackey has a persistent hamstring injury that will take "a little time." Spence has a leg injury for which he has been seen in a substantial knee brace.

"(Bryant is) going to have knee surgery, ACL repair," Lea said. "Unfortunately we lost him in the game against Delaware. I am just heartbroken for him. He has worked so hard and was having a great start to the season. ... Spence won't be with us on Saturday playing but we're encouraged with the progress he's making, so still week to week, not going to be this week, but if he continues to move forward the way he has, there's a chance that he could be available for something against Auburn."

Vanderbilt (2-0) will take on NC State (1-1) in its final non-conference game of the season on Sept. 19 (11:45 a.m. CT, SEC Network) before beginning SEC play. In that game, 5-star freshman quarterback Jared Curtis will get his first career start.

Spence has yet to play this season due to the injury but he has 25 receptions for 334 yards and four touchdowns across 29 career games played.

Lackey also has not played this season due to injury. Curtis recorded one tackle across two games played and Bryant appeared in two games but did not record any statistics.

Aria Gerson covers Vanderbilt athletics for The Tennessean. Contact her at agerson@gannett.com or on X @aria_gerson.

title: Sun Devils, except coach Kenny Dillingham, soaking up London ahead of Union Jack Classic
description: LONDON – Featuring ornate, architectural marvels and historic sites dating back centuries, this isn’t a city that should be explored in a hotel room – unless you’re Arizona State football...
fullText:
LONDON – Featuring ornate, architectural marvels and historic sites dating back centuries, this isn't a city that should be explored in a hotel room – unless you're Arizona State football coach Kenny Dillingham.

After a long trip across the pond, the Sun Devils' head man said that he had spent roughly 48 hours indoors at the team hotel, sequestered in his room like a hermit to prepare for Arizona State's game at Wembley Stadium against Kansas in the Union Jack Classic on Saturday. Kickoff is at 9 a.m. MST.

With the sun peeking through gray London skies, Dillingham finally caught a whiff of fresh outside air at ASU's Tuesday morning practice. Don't get any ideas. Dillingham said it won't be happening much this week, at least when it comes to non-team-related activities.

"I didn't sleep the first 36 hours I was here," Dillingham said. "I've been locked in a cave.

"My job is to get the best plan in place, and I (have) got to do the same process I do throughout a week. … We'll go to the Thursday event that we (have) got down there in London, but I don't plan on doing anything other than being in this hotel."

While Dillingham isn't keen to explore the city, he has encouraged his team to enjoy the unique experience of playing in an international game – a historic one at that, considering that it's the first-ever college football game in London to feature two FBS teams.

"I told them today, they're not hostages here," Dillingham said. "If you want to go do something, go do something. Just make sure we get what we need to get accomplished."

It's been a taxing turnaround for Dillingham's squad. Fresh off a 48-20 loss in College Station to No. 9 Texas A&M on Sept. 12, the Sun Devils flew straight to London for the back half of a roughly week-and-a-half-long stretch on the road.

The trip presents some obvious logistical hurdles – shipping a football team and its gear thousands of miles away isn't a straightforward task. Conversely, it provides ASU's players and staff with a chance to escape from football and create memorable moments as a team.

"No way would I want our team to fly across the country Week 3 to play this game," Dillingham said. "But this is an experience. They're still college athletes and I wasn't going to rob them of an experience to fly them across the country, go see London, be able to experience things and play in a stadium that's like a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity."

Veterans such as offensive tackle Jalen Klemm and defensive tackle C.J. Fite have kept busy, visiting local landmarks and trying one of England's most popular dishes for the first time: fish and chips.

"We have been taking the last couple of days to kind of acclimate to everything," Klemm said. "All of us have walked the grounds here and looked at everything. I know that on Thursday we have a boat ride that we're going to be able to go on and see a lot of the sights. So I know the guys are pretty excited for that."

For the most part, Dillingham has entrusted his players with the freedom to explore London on their own. Well, at least with a buddy. Or three.

Behind the program's pillars – which include, Fite noted being a good person and having safeguards like the buddy system in place – older players such as Fite and Klemm haven't felt the need to heavily monitor the younger players to prevent them from making poor decisions.

"Coach told us if you want to go out, you have to have three people with you," Fite said. "So if somebody wants to make a bad decision, three other people can stop them. There's certain things that you do, and that you already know, that kind of stop you from making those decisions. But all the guys kind of know already."

Like any trip abroad, it hasn't been smooth sailing for everyone. Klemm said his teammate, sophomore offensive lineman Manamo'ui Muti, found himself in a precarious position early in the week: locked in the hotel bathroom.

"It was pretty funny," Klemm said. "We went in there and we were knocking on the door and he was like, 'Hey guys,' and he was sending us videos from inside.

"Thankfully, he had his phone. I asked him what he would have done if he didn't have his phone. He was like, 'I might have had to break the door down.'"

While it seems the Devils are enjoying their time across the pond, they still remain aligned with their uber-focused coach, pledging not to let distractions get in the way of their main goal.

"At the end of the day, we came here to play a football game," Klemm said. "We got to keep the main thing the main thing."

title: 🐐 Scaloni calls up Messi: the No 10 gets his big send-off in Argentina
description: The Argentina national team officially announced the list of players called up by Lionel Scaloni for a three-match slate of international friendlies in the country, to be played between September 21 a...
fullText:
The Argentina national team officially announced the list of players called up by Lionel Scaloni for a three-match slate of international friendlies in the country, to be played between September 21 and October 6.

The first match for La Albiceleste will take place inland. On Wednesday, September 30, the national team will face Bolivia at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium in the province of Córdoba.

Afterward, Scaloni's squad will move its training camp to Buenos Aires for the remaining two matches at River Plate's stadium. On Saturday, October 3, they will take on Burkina Faso, before closing out the international window on Tuesday, October 6, against the Benin national team.

Rumors had already been circulating since the morning in Argentina that Scaloni was going to call up Lionel Messi so he could have his big farewell, and that will indeed happen on October 6 when they host Benin at the Monumental.

title: NBA commissioner admits Clippers discipline incidentally 'punishing the fans'
description: NBA commissioner Adam Silver expanded on a handful of hot-button topics.
fullText:
NEW YORK — NBA commissioner Adam Silver said the punishment of the Los Angeles Clippers for their role in circumventing the salary cap is final and was meant as a deterrent for other teams not to engage in breaking league rules.

Silver discussed some of the league's pressing matters as they concluded the two-day Board of Governors meeting in midtown Manhattan, while preparing for their 81st season starting Oct. 20, when the New York Knicks begin their defense of the championship against the Philadelphia 76ers.

Los Angeles had five first-round picks taken away, was fined $30 million, and Clippers owner Steve Ballmer was suspended from all league and team activities for one year for what the NBA said was the team "knowingly seeking to help" star forward Kawhi Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities.

Two other Clippers executives were suspended, and Leonard was fined $700,000 for their roles in the scheme; they were not represented at this Board of Governors meeting. Ballmer apologized to the team's fans and said in a statement he won't fight the won't fight salary-cap circumvention penalties.

Silver said during a press conference that there was difficulty in punishing the team, but there had to be "competitive consequences" for rule violations, and he doesn't think that he has done permanent damage to the franchise.

"We still want to be a 30-team league, and we recognize that, in some ways, we're unfortunately punishing the fans of that team as well. And so that's the balance we're trying to seek," Silver said. "The ultimate goal, in terms of these type of sanctions, are to ensure that other teams don't have to engage in this type of behavior, in the future, so there has to be something beyond suspensions and financial consequences, and that has to be to regulate competition"

The Clippers concluded the June 30 trade that sent Leonard back to the Toronto Raptors, where he helped win the NBA championship in 2019, for forward Brandon Ingram, guard Gradey Dick, as well as two unprotected first-round picks, one first-round pick swap, and two second-round selections. That deal had been on hold at the team's discretion while the NBA concluded its investigation into the Clippers.

Silver also updated the situation with the Los Angeles Lakers, which is being sold by Los Angeles Dodgers co-owner and TWG Global CEO Mark Walter for a record $12.5 billion to businessman Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger.

Lakers controlling owner Jeanie Buss is challenging that sale, saying her five siblings don't have the right to sell the family's 17.8% remaining stake in the team. Buss, by virtue of having more than 15% ownership of the team, remains the Lakers' governor.

Silver said he had no prior knowledge that Walter, whom federal prosecutors are investigating for potential financial improprieties at two insurance companies he controlled, wanted to sell the team until he heard from buyers who had a handshake deal with him. When dealing with Walter, Silver said the league found no red flags when he originally bought the team in October 2025.

"Even to this day, as you know, these are allegations," Silver said. There are issues that are now being looked into, but independent of Mark Walter choosing to sell this team right now, he was not being investigated by our league."

Silver discussed the potential league expansion into Las Vegas and Seattle, as well as the situation in Portland with the Trail Blazers, where the fight for a new arena drags on under owner Thomas Dundon.

Silver made it clear that the team needs a new arena to replace the Moda Center, which opened in 1995 and is considered one of the league's worst venues. He added that they haven't discussed the team relocating and that it would be a "failure" if the team moved.

"It is important, at the same time, that Tom Dundon reaches a deal with the city officials and the state elected officials that makes operating important and viable for the long term. So that's what we're focused on."

There is no timetable for the expansion of the new teams, the last of which was added in 2004 with the Charlotte Bobcats, bringing the league's total to 30. The Bobcats were renamed the Hornets a decade later.

As far as Vegas and Seattle, Silver said the next round of bids will be coming in shortly.

"I think that there is real excitement around either, you know, a renovated T-Mobile Arena," Silver said of Vegas. "I think it still needs some significant improvements, but at the same time, there are groups who have presented plans to go, what I would call, you know, a modern entertainment palace in Las Vegas, and it's a unique market."

title: Concern around Brandon Aubrey feels fair right now
description: Are you at all concerned about Brandon Aubrey right now?
fullText:
Brandon Aubrey missed an extra point on Sunday night against the New York Giants. No harm, no foul. Extra points are missed all of the time in the NFL, right? We shouldn't be freaking out over a single kick. This isn't like early in Aubrey's career where he was automatic and the out-of-nowhere miss was almost funny because it was so rare.

The thing is, we are definitely not in those days anymore. There isn't any real need to panic at this point in time, but Brandon Aubrey's misses are becoming a bit of a thing now. And that has to be discussed.

It should be noted that the extra point that Brandon Aubrey missed was made more difficult by the extra yardage applied to it following Javonte Williams' ridiculous taunting penalty. It was literally harder than your average extra point is the overall point.

Aubrey struggled in his most recent NFL game before Sunday night, last season's finale which was also against the Giants at MetLife Stadium. In fact, Aubrey has now missed a kick of some kind in three straight games.

This is the first time in his career that this is the case.

Again, no one is suggesting panic. Aubrey has a very large body of work that suggests this all might be an aberration, even if admittedly a sort of a large aberration which is a bit of an oxymoron.

It bears mentioning that the last two games took place in the same stadium, MetLife, and that it is outdoors and also known for not having the most quality playing surface in the NFL. None of these things are excuses, to be clear. They are simply data points in talking about the overall subject at large.

When you throw out terms like "concern" and "worried" people tend to take them at their most intense definitions. It is fair to say that you, me, or anyone is concerned/worried about Aubrey given his recent form, but that doesn't have to mean that we are ready to totally freak out.

So you be the judge. How concerned and/or worried are you? A lot? A little? None at all?

title: Paul George has no ill will toward Boston Celtics fans over Jaylen Brown trade reception
description: "To be honest, they should have a relationship emotionally to that trade," said George.
fullText:
Paul George is no Jaylen Brown, and the former Philadelphia 76ers veteran forward made it clear he harbors no ill will towards fans of the Boston Celtics who were less than thrilled about his joining the team via the trade that sent the Georgia native to the Sixers earlier this offseason.

Speaking to the media at his introductory press conference on Tuesday (Sep. 15) afternoon, George opened up about the initial ire over the trade by many a Boston fan. "Listen, I understand the circumstances. I understand how huge JB was not only for the organization, but here in the city," began PG-13, "so I didn't take it personal."

"To be honest, they should have a relationship emotionally to that trade," continued the 16-season veteran with a nod to Brown's legacy with the Celtics.

"But my job here is (to) come in, it's a great opportunity for me," said George. "Obviously the last two years have been rough with injuries, but for myself personally, I feel great again."

"I feel like I've turned that corner of dealing with injuries and now re-establishing myself and from a physical standpoint again. And with that, I can carry it over to the court. So, again, no personal feelings towards the initial ... how it (was) received in here in Boston."

"To be honest, it's fair, but one foot in front of the other, hopefully with how we start this year, they understand this is a new team and something that they can be proud of," said the new Boston wing.

title: Holly Rowe reveals private talk with Arch Manning after AI video backlash
description: One day after calling the viral video "hilarious," the Texas QB acknowledged that his reaction caused harm.
fullText:
Texas Longhorns star quarterback Arch Manning published an apology on Tuesday afternoon following his response to a viral AI video that depicted his head coach slapping a female journalist.

Manning's apology focused on his back-and-forth with reporters on Monday about a social media post featuring an AI-generated video showing Longhorns head coach Sarkisian slapping ESPN reporter Holly Rowe, and Manning was asked if he'd seen it.

"I saw an AI edit of Sark's interview," Manning said, laughing. "That's a good one - of him slapping Holly Rowe. That's hilarious."

After morning practice, Manning took to Instagram stories to make his apology public.

"In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video," Manning's statement reads. "There is nothing funny about it. It's easy to say I didn't mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that."

Texas QB Arch Manning has apologized to Holly Rowe for his comments at Monday's press conference. #HookEm pic.twitter.com/YJHwHUt0Qu

Manning also acknowledged Rowe by name in the post.

"I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments," Manning wrote. "I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward."

Rowe responded to Manning's post on Instagram, acknowledging the apology and sharing that the two had a conversation about the matter.

"Thank you Arch. I appreciate our conversation about this, which will remain private. Apology accepted," Rowe replied on Instagram. "We move forward with respect and kindness for one another."

Manning, 22, is currently the star junior quarterback for a Longhorns team that just moved up to No. 1 in the AP Top 25 Poll on Monday. Peyton and Eli Manning's nephew will hopefully have better, more mature days on the microphone in future press conferences.

However, what's unique here is that Manning spoke about managing his experiences with the media and what he learned from Peyton and his grandfather, Archie Manning, right before making the controversial comments about the AI-produced video.

"I guess subconsciously seeing them do interviews and press conferences definitely took stuff from them," Manning said during Monday's press conference. "I think my dad and my grandfather saying, 'This guy looks like an idiot talking about this or this guy does a good job.' So just hearing bits and pieces of what they think and trying to apply it."

Arch Manning on learning how to deal with the media from uncle's Peyton and Eli. pic.twitter.com/6p01qzcrvA

Hopefully Manning will apply this learning moment and put it into practice going forward.

title: Rory McIlroy reveals what he told Shane Lowry after his Irish Open win, ’it was amazing to see’
description: Rory McIlroy has revealed that he reminded Shane Lowry that class is permanent after watching his great friend win the Irish Open by 11 shots on Sunday. Lowry certainly helped out anyone who was keen to predominantly watch the Solheim Cup this past week as he quickly took complete control at Doonbeg.
fullText:
Rory McIlroy has revealed that he reminded Shane Lowry that class is permanent after watching his great friend win the Irish Open by 11 shots on Sunday.

Lowry certainly helped out anyone who was keen to predominantly watch the Solheim Cup this past week as he quickly took complete control at Doonbeg. He ended up winning by 11 shots after rolling in a long birdie putt on the 72nd hole to send the crowd into a frenzy.

Remarkably, it was Lowry's first individual victory on either the PGA Tour or DP World Tour since 2022. And of course, this season has been a difficult one for the 39-year-old after he failed to get across the line at both the Dubai Invitational and the Cognizant Classic with the tournaments within his grasp.

The collapse at PGA National seemed to knock Lowry's confidence for some time. He failed to finish inside the top 25 at any of the four majors, while he also did not make it past the first FedEx Cup playoff event.

However, he was able to put that disappointment behind him on home turf, with Rory McIlroy among those who were delighted for the 2019 Open Championship winner.

Speaking to the media ahead of the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth, McIlroy opened up on some of the support he has given Lowry throughout the season.

"Still a long way to go. Like I said to Shane afterwards, on Sunday, form is temporary and class is permanent. He is that calibre of a player we all know he is. It was just a matter of him getting back to that point and winning a tournament," he said.

"I think him finishing it off in emphatic style the way he did, I think it will do a lot for him, and it will hopefully do a lot for him with how he approaches final rounds going forward because I think he would admit himself that final rounds have been a struggle over the last couple years for him.

"But I think for him to go out, shoot 63 on the final day leading your national Open with all that crowd support behind you, he really went out there, and he grabbed the tournament by the throat and made it his. It was amazing to see.

"He alluded to it on Sunday night as well. He's had some hard times this year, and we've had some chats and heart-to-hearts about it. All I can try to be is a good friend and provide encouragement and maybe provide examples of what I've tried to do in those circumstances.

"Yeah, as I said, I think it was only a matter of time. It was amazing to see."

It should not surprise anyone if Lowry and McIlroy end up battling it out for the title at the DP World Tour's flagship event over the coming days.

Lowry actually finished second to McIlroy back in 2014, while the roles were reversed eight years later when it was Lowry who emerged victorious.

And speaking after his final round four years ago, McIlroy explained why he was delighted to see Lowry win if he was not going to be able to.

"I'm so happy for him. He's played a lot of great golf this year. I think back to he had a chance at the Honda, got screwed with that big downpour on 17 and 18. Hilton Head as well, playing in the final group with Harold Varner. He's had a lot of chances to win this year and hasn't quite got over the line," he said.

"I'm really happy for him. He's played a lot of good golf and he deserves this one. I wish I would have made him play a couple extra holes maybe to get the trophy but incredibly happy for Shane and hopefully we'll have a couple drinks tonight."

Interestingly, McIlroy alluded to Lowry just missing out on the title at the event now known as the Cognizant Classic.

With Lowry getting that win last week, perhaps it should not be a big shock if history really does repeat itself and he manages to triumph at Wentworth.

title: Colby Donovan’s Celtic breakthrough earns Scotland call up
description: Colby Donovan’s rapid rise at Celtic has been rewarded with a first call-up to the senior Scotland squad. In the announcement earlier on Tuesday, Sébastien Pocognoli confirmed a place for the Celti...
fullText:
Colby Donovan's rapid rise at Celtic has been rewarded with a first call-up to the senior Scotland squad. In the announcement earlier on Tuesday, Sébastien Pocognoli confirmed a place for the Celtic defender in his revamped squad.

The academy graduate has firmly established himself as a first-team option, initially benefiting from Alistair Johnston's injury before producing performances which have increasingly justified his place in Martin O'Neill's plans.

Donovan has now accumulated 37 senior appearances for Celtic across domestic and European competition, contributing four assists. Ten of those outings have arrived this season, including six in the Premiership, underlining his growing importance within the squad.

13th September 2026; Ibrox Stadium, Glasgow, Scotland; Scottish League Cup Football, Rangers versus Celtic; Djeidi Gassama of Rangers challenges Colby Donovan of Celtic

Despite Sunday's disappointing 3-0 defeat at Ibrox, the right-back was one of Celtic's more encouraging performers. His excellent early pass released Kasper Høgh and offered a glimpse of the composure and quality he has increasingly demonstrated at senior level.

That progress has now been recognised by new Scotland manager Pocognoli, who has included Donovan among the uncapped players in his first senior squad.

For Celtic, it represents another significant milestone in the development of one of the club's brightest academy prospects. Donovan was handed his opportunity and, rather than simply providing temporary cover, has increasingly looked capable of establishing himself as a long-term first-team player.
